newsitem.title: UK: Asian fund portfolios beat index in 2Q.
newsitem.headline: Asian fund portfolios beat index in 2Q.

text.p: Specialist Asian investment portfolios have outperformed the markets for the fourth consecutive quarter, according to a study by consultants WM Company.

The WM Asian Universe, which includes 21 investment portfolios worth $3 billion, shows an average return of 6.8 percent in the second quarter of 1997. This compares to a 5.1 percent return on the MSCI Far East All Countries Free ex-Japan index.
The main reason for the outperformance was fund managers' overweight position in Hong Kong, the region's best performer in the quarter, according to the study.
"Managers have done even better over the last year, producing an average return of 8.9 percent against an index return of only 2.8 percent," said Colin Kay, a WM Company director.
The study was done in conjunction with investment management consultants RCP & Partners.
